## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-29] Fred's investor tracking reads only US 13F filings, so it can't see the European holdings that make up most of his live book. Today's podcast pick puts a manager who owns the same kind of business in front of him.** [[finance/tracked-investors-candidates]] is built from Equibles' 13F data, and its candidates include two UK managers, Nick Train (Lindsell Train, 27 US positions, −16.2% QoQ) and Terry Smith (Fundsmith). A 13F lists only US-listed securities, so it misses what these managers hold in London and Amsterdam. That is where [[finance/trading-portfolio]] holds RELX (REL, 40 sh, +16%) and Wolters Kluwer (WKL, +19%), both information-services compounders of the kind Train is known for. Today's [[podcasts/suggestions]] pick, *The Value Perspective* (Schroders), has a Nick Train interview. The obvious workaround doesn't help: a check today of Equibles `GetMajorShareholdings` for XLON:REL returns only BlackRock (9.67%, 2022) and Invesco (2018), because FCA notifications start at 3% and no active manager crosses that in a £60bn+ company. `GetEuropeanFundHoldings` covers only Swedish UCITS. **Next step:** (1) for UK/EU managers, use their own monthly factsheets as the holdings source, e.g. Finsbury Growth & Income Trust's top-10 (Lindsell Train) and Fundsmith Equity's top-10. Check whether REL, WKL, SAP or another live name appears there, and treat any change as a signal like a 13F change. (2) Mark in the candidates page that the 13F list cannot see non-US holdings, so a Train or Smith row says nothing about the European book. (3) If Fred listens to the Train episode, check whether Train's case for data/information businesses covers the AI-disruption risk that the 2026-09-29 connection found the risk table ignores for REL/WKL.

- **[2026-10-29] Books has had nothing logged as read for 12 weeks, so its recommender and summarizer are now working from a frozen history.** The last entry in [[books/reading-list]] is *Breath* (added 2026-08-03). Since then the book-summarizer has had nothing new to summarise (its last page was 09-01), and the book-recommender's July–October batches (16 picks, including *Number Go Up*, *The Most Dangerous Trade* and *Off the Scales*, which other connections in this file depend on) are still based on the May–August list. [[books/books-from-podcasts]] has also grown to 26 titles, and only one is marked read. The 2026-10-25 idea called Cooking "the only recommender that never learns what Fred did". Books now has the same problem in practice: its feedback is Fred's manual `/add-book`, and that stopped in August. Nothing in raw/ looks like a Kindle or Goodreads export that could fill the gap. **Next step:** ask Fred whether he has finished books since August that weren't logged (the Slow Horses run stopped at book 8, *Bad Actors*, and book 9 is the natural next one). If yes, add them; if he logs reading elsewhere (Goodreads/Kindle/StoryGraph), drop an export into raw/books/ so book-summarizer can pick it up. Either way, have the 11-15 book-recommender run state the date its reading-history snapshot was taken.
